http://www.euronews.com/2026/08/09/over-.text: China's east coast has been preparing for the storm's arrival in recent days, with work and transport services suspended in some areas along its predicted path.The centre of the typhoon moved over the coastline near Yuhuan City in Zhejiang Province at about 5:30 pm (09:30 GMT), China's National Meteorological Centre said in an online post.Maximum wind speeds near the centre were more than 150 kilometres per hour at the time it made landfall, the NMC said. Parts of central and eastern Zhejiang could receive 250 to 500 mm of rain.Authorities relocated more than 900,000 residents from the city of Wenzhou and opened more than 1,000 emergency shelters.Nearly 1,400 flights in and out of Shanghai's two main passenger airports were cancelled on Sunday, state broadcaster CCTV reported.Hangzhou's airport in nearby Zhejiang province saw 270 inbound and outbound flights cancelled, the report said.Heavy rain, strong windsThe effects were felt as far away as Hong Kong on China's southern coast, where the weather observatory posted a record high temperature of 36.9°C, caused by warm air pushed over the city by Typhoon Dolphin.With the storm "moving towards the vicinity of Zhejiang and moving inland, its outer subsiding air will persistently bring extremely hot weather to the territory today to Tuesday", the Hong Kong Observatory said.Typhoon Dolphin brought heavy rain and strong winds to Japan's Okinawa before reaching China.Seven people in Okinawa suffered minor injuries, including a man aged over 100 who was blown over by gusts, fell to the ground, and hit his head, according to the island's government.By Sunday afternoon, 5,290 households in Okinawa were without electricity, according to regional utility Okinawa Electric Power.In Taiwan, dozens of ferry services were suspended, and more than 180 flights were cancelled as the storm brought downpours and strong winds to the island's north on Sunday.Red alert issuedChina's NMC issued a red typhoon alert — its most severe warning — on Sunday morning, forecasting "extraordinary torrential rain" in some areas of central and eastern Zhejiang.Heavy precipitation is also expected to fall in Shanghai and parts of Fujian, Anhui and Jiangsu provinces through Monday afternoon, it said.Typhoon Dolphin was expected to weaken after making landfall while moving in a northwesterly direction over eastern China.In Fujian, nearly 99,000 people were relocated from "risky areas" on Saturday evening ahead of the storm's arrival, state news agency Xinhua reported.Services on more than 200 ferry routes were suspended in Zhejiang and Fujian, Xinhua said. Work on offshore projects was halted, while 474 construction vessels had been called to port by Friday morning, Xinhua said.Some train services in affected areas were also suspended on Sunday to ensure passenger safety, state media reported.Scientists say human-driven climate change is making extreme heat events more frequent and more intense worldwide.Typhoon Dolphin's arrival in China comes two weeks after Typhoon Noul lashed southern Guangdong province, declared by authorities at the time as the strongest storm to hit China this year.Three people were killed, and hundreds of homes were damaged by Typhoon Noul in the Philippines before it reached China.

https://hungarytoday.hu/defense-forces-p.text: Defense Forces Provide Drinking Water During Historic Heatwave A prolonged heatwave and historically low water levels in the Danube have led to drinking water supply problems in Szentendre, Pest County. To prevent shortages for residents, the Hungarian Defense Forces are supporting the local water supply effort. Soldiers from the Szentendre Garrison Support Command have stepped in to help civilians and have been coordinating a large-scale logistics operation for several days. To personally assess the situation and the relief efforts, Acting President Ágnes Forsthoffer, Defense Minister Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi, and Colonel General Zsolt Sándor, Chief of the Hungarian Defense Forces General Staff, visited the emergency logistics operation on site, honvedelem.hu reported. The visit began at the Budapest Waterworks facility, where the delegation was briefed on the process of filling the tanker trucks being used in the operation. The government and military officials then travelled to Szentendre, where they discussed the current situation and the next steps with Balázs Tóthmajor, the member of parliament for Pest County’s Constituency 4. The defense forces have been working intensively for days to resolve the water shortage,” Defense Minister Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi said on his social media page. He said that the return of drinking water to many households was thanks to the tireless efforts of Hungarian soldiers. “I am proud of them, and I hope the whole country is as well,” the minister added. The minister also stressed that during periods of extreme heat and the current energy crisis, the most important task is to provide help where it is needed most. “Our soldiers and water transport vehicles are working day and night to maintain the safe drinking water supply of the population. Over 2 million liters of water have already been delivered, and the work continues without interruption,” he said. Sztaniszláv Horváth/honvedelem.hu Acting President Ágnes Forsthoffer also expressed her thanks and praised the efforts of those involved in the emergency response. The operation is not limited to Szentendre. In addition to continuous drinking water deliveries by tanker trucks, the defense forces are supporting emergency supplies in several regions. The Defense Ministry announced on Wednesday that the available stock of packaged drinking water had reached nearly 45,000 bags. Sztaniszláv Horváth/honvedelem.hu A boy cools himself with bagged drinking water delivered by the Hungarian Defense Forces’ unit in Szentes. Photo: MTI/Szigetváry Zsolt In Budapest’s 21st District, 1,000 water bags will be distributed daily on Thursday and Friday. In the 11th District, collection points at Bikás Park and Móricz Zsigmond Square had already received 600 bags each. Drinking water is being transported from Szár to the reservoir at Csabdi-Vasztélypuszta. Continuous deliveries are also underway from Budapest to Szentendre and from Pócsmegyer to Tahitótfalu. The logistics operation highlights the role of the defense forces in responding to civilian emergencies. Soldiers will remain on site and continue securing supplies until local public infrastructure has been fully stabilized. On Monday, Hungary was one of the hottest countries in Europe. Europe Home page Europe 0 0 Romania could lose EU funds over delay in shutting coal-fired power plants 12 August 2026 06:06 (UTC +04:00) Romania could risk losing access to European funds as it seeks to postpone the closure of coal-fired power plants amid mounting pressure on the country's electricity system. Romanian media reported that the government wants to delay the planned shutdowns after the second reactor at the Cernavodă Nuclear Power Plant, the country's only nuclear power station, was taken offline. Romanian Energy Ministry State Secretary Cristian Bușoi outlined the country's difficult energy situation during a meeting of the European Commission's Electricity Coordination Group. He said Romania activated an early warning mechanism last Friday before declaring a "crisis situation" on Monday evening. Bușoi warned that the planned shutdown of Unit 5 at the Turceni coal-fired power plant, part of Romania's energy market reform commitments, could create additional difficulties under the current circumstances. He asked the European Commission to allow four generating units at the plant to continue operating beyond August. The Romanian official also proposed assessing the capacity of neighboring countries' power systems and cross-border electricity interconnections to determine how they could support Romania in the event of a worsening energy crisis. Romania's attempt to keep its coal-fired generation capacity operating longer than previously agreed could, however, put at risk European funding linked to the country's energy transition and reform commitments. https://www.just-auto.com/news/aumovio-c.text: The business develops and manufactures cleaning systems including window washers, camera, sensor and headlamp cleaning systems. Credit: Marcelo Trad/Shutterstock.com AUMOVIO has agreed to sell its washer and cleaning business to Munich-based industrial holding company CERTINA Group, as the automotive supplier continues to streamline its portfolio and focus capital on core technologies. The deal, announced on 3 September, covers production, research and development, employees and all related business activities. Find out more Closing is subject to customary conditions and is expected by the end of 2026. The companies did not disclose the purchase price. The business is headquartered in Adrspach and operates entirely in the Czech Republic, employing around 700 people. It develops and manufactures cleaning systems including window washers, camera, sensor and headlamp cleaning systems, as well as fluid supply products. AUMOVIO CEO Philipp von Hirschheydt said: “The sale is another step in our larger strategy to focus on our core business. This means shifting our resources to technologies we have identified as the growth and value drivers for AUMOVIO.” CERTINA plans to integrate the business into its automotive platform, which generates around €600m in annual revenue. CERTINA Group automotive division head Dr Stefan Brungs said: “The business is a perfect fit for our automotive division. With its strong team in Adrspach, its proven technology and its long-standing customer relationships, the business has everything it needs to grow as an independent company.” The disposal follows other portfolio actions by AUMOVIO, including the sale of its Mechelen site in Belgium to Dumarey Group and a previously announced plan to cut up to 4,000 jobs globally by the end of 2026 in an R&D overhaul. The move comes as AUMOVIO works through a weaker first half and the effects of its BMW settlement related to a warranty claim. In the first half of 2026, AUMOVIO reported sales of €8.65bn ($10.05bn), down 9.4% year on year and 8.9% on adjusted basis. EBIT worsened to a loss of €469m from a loss of €144m, while earnings before tax declined to a loss of €569m from a loss of €95m. Net income attributable to shareholders was a loss of €597m, versus a loss of €232m in the prior-year period. Sign up for our daily news round-up! https://www.crash.net/wsbk/news/1105855/.text: Nicolo Bulega crosses the line to win the WorldSBK title in Race 2 at Cremona. © Gold & Goose Prefer Crash.Net on Google See our stories more often Add Nicolo Bulega’s WorldSBK title is a crowning moment not only for the man himself but also for his bike, the undefeated Ducati Panigale V4 R. Bulega himself has been undeniably excellent in the 2026 WorldSBK season. After 30 races, he has nine poles out of 10, 26 race wins, no DNFs, and 30 podiums. He hasn’t finished outside the top-two all season, indeed not since 2024 in dry races. At the same time, the bike he’s ridden, the 2026 Ducati Panigale V4 R, has taken WorldSBK to a different level of performance. It has won all 30 races, every podium position since Race 2 at the Hungarian Round in May, and holds the first three positions in the riders’ standings – and seven of the first 10. As a result, while Ducati Corse general manager Gigi Dall’Igna praised Bulega after he won the title, the Italian engineer also wanted to make sure bike got the credit it deserves. Nicolo Bulega, 2026 Italian WorldSBK, podium. Credit: Gold and Goose. © Gold & Goose Article continues below ADVERTISEMENT Article continues below ADVERTISEMENT “I’m really proud about Nicolo’s [Bulega] job this year, but also about all the people that worked on this bike: the teams, the guys that worked at Borgo Panigale,” Dall’Igna told WorldSBK.com after Race 2 at Cremona. “Everybody did an amazing job and I’m really proud for them.” Dall’Igna added: “He [Bulega] won almost all the races of the 2026 season, so for sure he did an unbelievable job.
